stem: Which tool is a web-based graphical console for building, managing and monitoring Azure resources, including custom dashboards?
why_correct: The Azure portal is a web-based, unified console that gives a graphical alternative to command-line tools.
why_a_wrong: Azure CLI is a command-line tool that uses Bash commands.
why_b_wrong: AzCopy is a command-line utility for copying blobs or files.
why_d_wrong: Azure Arc extends Azure management to resources outside Azure and is not a console.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe Azure Cloud Shell, including Azure Command-Line Interface (CLI) and Azure PowerShell
stem: An administrator is on a borrowed laptop with nothing installed and needs to run Azure CLI commands from the browser. Which service should they use?
why_correct: Azure Cloud Shell is a browser-based shell for managing Azure resources, and it supports both Azure PowerShell and the Azure CLI without installing anything locally.
why_b_wrong: Azure Arc manages resources outside Azure and is not a shell.
why_c_wrong: Azure Advisor gives recommendations about your resources and does not run commands.
why_d_wrong: Azure File Sync keeps a Windows file server synced with Azure Files.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe Azure Cloud Shell, including Azure Command-Line Interface (CLI) and Azure PowerShell
stem: Which statement about Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell is correct?
option_a: The CLI uses Bash commands and PowerShell uses cmdlets
option_b: Azure PowerShell can only run on Windows
option_c: Azure CLI can only be used inside the Azure portal
option_d: Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell cannot do the same tasks
why_correct: Azure CLI and Azure PowerShell are functionally equivalent. The main difference is syntax: the CLI uses Bash commands and PowerShell uses cmdlets.
why_b_wrong: Both can be installed on Windows, Linux and Mac, and also run in Cloud Shell.
why_c_wrong: The CLI can be installed on Windows, Linux and Mac as well as used in Cloud Shell.
why_d_wrong: They handle the same tasks, so the choice mostly depends on which language you know.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe the purpose of Azure Arc
stem: A company has servers in its own datacenter and virtual machines in another cloud. It wants to manage them with Azure management tools from one place. Which service fits?
why_correct: Azure Arc extends Azure management and governance to on-premises and multicloud resources, projecting them into Azure Resource Manager so they can be managed like Azure resources.
why_a_wrong: Advisor gives recommendations for your Azure resources and does not manage outside resources.
why_c_wrong: Cloud Shell is a browser-based shell, not a management platform for other clouds.
why_d_wrong: Service Health reports outages and maintenance that affect your Azure services.
author: claude

stem: A team wants identical test and production environments that can be deployed again and again from files, instead of clicking through the portal each time. Which approach fits?
why_correct: Infrastructure as code manages infrastructure through code and templates instead of manual configuration, which gives repeatable environment deployments.
why_a_wrong: Manual portal work is the opposite of repeatable deployment from files.
why_c_wrong: Service Health alerts tell you about outages and maintenance and do not deploy anything.
why_d_wrong: Advisor recommendations suggest improvements and do not deploy environments.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe Azure Resource Manager (ARM) and ARM templates
stem: What is an Azure Resource Manager (ARM) template?
option_a: A JSON file that declares the Azure resources to deploy
option_b: A command-line utility for copying blobs
option_d: A report of current Azure outages
why_correct: An ARM template is a JSON file that describes in declarative form the Azure resources you want to deploy.
why_b_wrong: Copying blobs is what AzCopy does, not an ARM template.
why_c_wrong: A browser-based shell is Azure Cloud Shell.
why_d_wrong: Outage information comes from Azure Service Health.
author: claude

objective_text: Describe Azure Resource Manager (ARM) and ARM templates
stem: Which Azure service receives requests from the portal, the CLI, PowerShell and the SDKs, then authenticates and authorizes them?
why_correct: Azure Resource Manager is the deployment and management service for Azure. Requests from any Azure tool go through it, so results are consistent.
why_a_wrong: Azure Monitor collects and analyzes monitoring data.
why_b_wrong: Azure Arc extends management to resources outside Azure.
why_d_wrong: Azure Advisor gives recommendations and does not process management requests.
author: claude
